newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN leaders urge business to cash in on growth.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN leaders urge business to cash in on growth.

text.p: Southeast Asian leaders urged world businesses on Wednesday to take advantage of the region's progress towards a borderless economy and the explosive growth that it was forecast to stimulate.

Indonesian President Suharto, opening a two-day meeting of global business leaders, said the region was likely to have one of the highest growth rates in the world in the early part of the next century.
"ASEAN (the Association of Southeast Asian Nations) will become one of the regions with the highest economic growth in the world in the decades to come," Suharto told the first ASEAN Business summit.

"As a result, a synergy is necessary -- whether between the government and businessmen, amongst ASEAN businessmen themselves and between ASEAN and non-ASEAN businessmen," he said. "This is achieved...by seizing opportunities within ASEAN and even outside ASEAN."
Some 600 business leaders from 30 countries, including about 200 from the United States, are attending the two-day summit in Jakarta.

Participants have said that with the adoption of an ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) by 2003 and liberalisation of trade between Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) countries by 2020, the region should record explosive growth in the early part of the 21st century.
They have said Southeast Asia should have one billion consumers and $2.0 trillion in combined gross domestic product by 2020, up from the current 400 million and about $600 billion respectively.
ASEAN comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam and Brunei. Cambodia, Laos and Burma are expected to join the bloc this year.

"AFTA is the first step towards what should eventually be a borderless ASEAN economic region," said Malaysian Trade Minister Rafidah Aziz. "It is hoped that in the future, the ASEAN economic entity will not merely be seen as a free trade area but as a dynamic global hub.

"The next step is to widen the scope of AFTA and to add on other ASEAN regional schemes to boost and complement AFTA," she added. She said the private sector could be responsible for creating one possible ancilliary scheme -- setting up ASEAN conglomerates which could take advantage of complementing business in the region to make inroads into the global economy.
"Such consortia, with the requisite capital and synergistic strength, can and will attract the large international players as partners," Aziz said.

Former U.S. Secretary of State Alexander Haig, who headed the U.S. business delegation to the meeting, said the United States, the largest trading partner of the region, would strengthen its economic ties with ASEAN.
"Southeast Asia is clearly the fastest growing market in the world," he said.

"Our mission is to highlight the American business community's long-term commitment to partnership with ASEAN and also to identify new business opportunities that will continue to invite even more investment in the next century."
